evidence.text: Reason for referral: Evaluation of exertional dyspnea and reduced exercise tolerance over four months in a 71-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease stage 3a, hypertension, and a brother with a heart attack at age 66.

A resting 12-lead ECG was obtained in the clinic today and showed sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, normal axis, first-degree AV block with a PR interval of 224 ms, QRS 96 ms, QTc 438 ms, and nonspecific T-wave flattening in the lateral leads. No prior tracing was available for comparison.

Findings: Normal left ventricular size with mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Left ventricular ejection fraction estimated at 55 to 60%. Grade 1 diastolic dysfunction. No significant valve disease. No pericardial effusion.
Impression: Preserved left ventricular systolic function with mild left ventricular hypertrophy and grade 1 diastolic dysfunction.
